title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is not Grothendieck's own text. It is page 78 of a typed English translation of what looks like a Soviet-school algebraic geometry text (phrasing such as 'biregular imbedding', 'cross-section of the variety', and the use of U^(i) for affine charts). It is misfiled among the 1965 'Galois theory of motives' notes; the neighbouring pages are Grothendieck's French manuscript on Tannakian categories of motives over R and F_q, with no mathematical connection. The handwritten '119' in the corner is the archive folio number.

Mathematical content (modern language). V is a projective variety of dimension s and E' is a divisor on V. For each n, f_n : V -> P^N is the rational map given by a basis φ_0,...,φ_r of H^0(V, O(nE')), and V^(n) is its image.

The first lines finish an argument that f_n is regular, i.e. defined everywhere. Near a point Q', some φ_k is nonzero, so the ratios φ_i/φ_k are regular there. Since F_2(Q') = F_2(Q) ≠ 0, the rational function R = F_1/F_2 is regular at Q'.

The main argument is the start of the proof that f_n is an embedding for large n, by induction on dim V:
- A hyperplane φ = 0 not containing V^(n) cuts V^(n) in a set that is the image of the divisor E_φ = (φ) + nE' on V. Locally E_φ is given by φ^(i) = 0 in the chart U^(i), and it has dimension s-1.
- By the induction hypothesis there is m = m(E_φ) such that H^0(E_φ, O(mE')|_{E_φ}) gives a closed embedding of E_φ.
- The exact sequence (19) is presumably 0 -> O((m-1)E') -> O(mE') -> O_{E_φ}(mE') -> 0, together with vanishing of H^1 for large m. It shows that restriction of sections is surjective, so this embedding of E_φ is just f_m restricted to E_φ.
- Hence f_m(E_φ) has dimension s-1. A hyperplane section of V^(m) therefore has dimension s-1, so dim V^(m) = s, i.e. f_m is generically finite.

This is a step toward proving that f_m is one-to-one and biregular. It is the classical inductive proof that an 'ample-type' divisor becomes very ample, in the spirit of the Kodaira/Serre/Nakai-type criteria as presented in Soviet expositions of the 1960s (e.g. the Shafarevich seminar literature). The exact source is uncertain.
errors: The surjectivity H^0(V, O(mE')) -> H^0(E_φ, O(mE')|E_φ) needs a vanishing H^1(V, O((m-1)E')) = 0 for large m (Serre vanishing or a hypothesis on E'). The page invokes 'exact sequence (19)' without restating this.

The induction hypothesis is applied to E_φ, which may be singular, reducible or non-reduced. The inductive statement must be formulated for that generality, and m(E_φ) depends on the choice of φ; the page does not address either point.
The concluding step only gives dim V^(m) = s, i.e. generic finiteness. Injectivity is announced but not proved on this page.

ideas.what: Inductive proof via hyperplane sections and a restriction exact sequence that the map defined by |mE'| is an embedding / has full-dimensional image
ideas.modern_name: very ampleness of multiples of an ample divisor; Lefschetz-type induction on hyperplane sections; Serre vanishing argument
ideas.usually_credited_to: Kodaira, Serre (FAC 1955), Nakai, Moishezon; standard textbook material
ideas.where_published: EGA II §4.5 and EGA III treat ampleness and very ampleness (in a different style)

deep.surprise_reason: A misfiled page of a typed English translation of someone else's classical algebraic geometry text (ampleness / projective embedding by induction on dimension). It has no connection to the surrounding Grothendieck notes on motives, and its content is standard.
transcription_corrections: Page is in English typescript, likely a translation of a Russian text, not Grothendieck's French manuscript.
'The equation φ^{m_e} = 0' is uncertain; it probably refers to the equation φ = 0 of a hyperplane (or φ^(n)); the superscript is unclear in the image.
'the equation E_φ in U^(i) - the set φ^(i) = 0' should read 'the equation of E_φ in U^(i) is the set φ^(i) = 0'.
'O_{E_φ}[mE']_{E_φ}' denotes the sheaf O(mE') restricted to E_φ.
Handwritten '119' at the lower left is the archive folio number.
